classification_categories.power_calc: Formal a priori power calculation (α, β, effect size specified)
classification_categories.effect_size_estimate: Quantitative estimate from pilot/literature, no formal calc
classification_categories.replication_standard: Appeal to field convention or replication of prior study
classification_categories.resource_constraint: Sample size limited by availability, budget, or cohort size
classification_categories.methodology_determined: Sample size inherently defined by measurement technique or study design (stereology, cryo-EM, single-molecule imaging, complete-specimen census); no separate determination step expected
classification_categories.no_justification: n stated but no reasoning provided
classification_categories.na_or_blank: Field empty, N/A, or not applicable
classification_categories.ambiguous: Text present but insufficient to classify

records.title: Gene-drive-capable mosquitoes suppress patient-derived malaria in Tanzania
records.sample_size_raw: No formal statistical power calculations were performed. Sample sizes were chosen based on prior similar experiments and logistical feasibility, ensuring sufficient biological replicates for statistical comparisons (e.g. mosquito fertility and fecundity, infection prevalence and intensity, oocyst size).

records.title: Mapping the genetic landscape across 14 psychiatric disorders
records.sample_size_raw: The current study reflects the largest and most comprehensive cross-disorder psychiatric genetic analysis to-date. This study makes use of the largest psychiatric disorder GWAS currently available. Sample sizes for each of the included 14 disorders are provided in Table 1 of the main text.

records.title: An RNA splicing system that excises DNA transposons from animal mRNAs
records.sample_size_raw: No statistical method was used to predetermine sample size. All quantitative data represent the mean of at least three independent experiments, as indicated by the data points shown in the graphs. For C. elegans assays, PCR was performed using samples collected from 60 mm plates of worms to obtain sufficient quantities of DNA or RNA. For fluorescence and RNAi phenotyping experiments, a minimum of 50 animals per experiment were analyzed, with each experiment repeated three times. In cases where homozygous animals were limited (Fig. 5g and Extended Data Fig. 10d, e, g), a minimum of 10 animals per experiment and three biological replicates were used. For cell line assays, PCR was performed using RNA extracted from 100 mm plates of cells at >80% confluency. For flow cytometry, approximately 10,000 individual cells per group were analyzed. Fluorescence imaging experiments were conducted with three biological replicates, with representative images shown. The sample sizes used in this study are consistent with standard practices in the field. (PMID: 31002798; 32499657)

records.title: Soft biodegradable implants for long-distance and wide-angle sensing
records.sample_size_raw: No statistical method was used to predetermine sample size. The sample sizes for each experiment were chosen based on the following rationales: * Cell toxicity (n=6 independent material-containing culture mediums): This sample size is consistent with common practice in the field for initial biocompatibility assessment and provides a robust basis for evaluating cytotoxicity. * Mouse toxicity (n=3 independent mice) & Rat toxicity (n=3 independent rats): These sample sizes were chosen for this pilot investigation to provide preliminary data on in vivo safety and feasibility, allowing for the observation of major adverse effects before considering larger-scale studies. * Mg content of rat organ and tissue (n=1 rat): The goal was not to study inter-animal variability, which is well-documented in the literature, but to confirm that the magnesium levels from our device fell within a normal physiological range.
